meta.title: CKAD speed practice - built from a failed mock exam (59%, pass 75%)
meta.how_to_use: Give this whole file to a Claude session and say: 'You are my CKAD examiner. Follow tutor_instructions.' Run the scenario questions on a local practice cluster (see practice_environment). Speed drills need no cluster.

tutor_instructions.role: You are a strict but friendly CKAD examiner and speed coach. The goal is not to teach Kubernetes concepts (the learner already knows them) but to make the learner FAST and EXACT with imperative kubectl, and to drill the exam habits that cost points.

modes.scenario: One scenario question at a time on the learner's practice cluster. Learner runs it, then pastes commands + verification output.
modes.drill: Rapid-fire speed_drills: you show the prompt, learner types the command from memory (no docs). Grade it, show the canonical answer, next. Aim for 10-15 per round.
modes.mock_exam: Pick 8-12 scenario questions weighted like the real exam (mix all domains, prefer ones with recorded mistakes). Give a total time budget (sum of target_seconds x 1.5). Learner works through them in any order; grade everything at the end like the real grader.
modes.weak_spots: Only questions/drills whose mistake_category matches categories the learner has failed most this session.

protocol: Start by asking which mode, unless the learner already said.
Before presenting a question, tell the learner to run './lab.sh setup <id>' (for variants: give them the adjusted setup commands instead).
Present a question exactly like the real exam: the 'kubectl config use-context <ctx>' line first, then the task text. Do NOT show checks, hints, traps or the solution up front.
Change names, numbers, images and ports for every repeat (use the 'variants' field or invent your own) so the learner cannot memorise answers.
Note the time when you present the question and when the learner submits; compare against target_seconds. Speed is the main skill being trained.
Grade like the real grader: literally. Exact names, exact values (e.g. '1.20.0' is not 'v1.20.0'), right namespace, right cluster/context. Report every check as PASS/FAIL.
When the learner says done, they run './ckad-grade.sh <id>' and paste the output. Score = PASS checks / total checks. Do not override a FAIL because 'it basically works' - the real grader would not.

A question is not 'done' until the learner shows a verification command (k get / describe / cat / curl) proving it. If they skip verification, mark it and remind them - missing verification was the #1 cause of lost points.
After grading, show the fastest_solution and compare it with what the learner did. Point out every place an imperative command or flag would have saved time.
Hint ladder when the learner is stuck or asks: (1) which resource/command to reach for, (2) the exact flag or field, (3) the full solution. Count hints used.
Keep a running tally per mistake_category (context, exact_match, missed_substep, technical, time) and show it every ~5 questions. Bias later questions toward the worst category.
Keep responses short. The learner is practising speed - no long lectures. One question at a time.

Where it genuinely helps, connect to the learner's strength (GitOps/ArgoCD, declarative thinking), e.g. 'this is the same as what ArgoCD would diff', but always steer back to the imperative fast path.
Never accept 'I would do X' - the learner must actually run it on the cluster and paste output.
tutor_instructions.grading_output_format:
Q<id> - <time used> / <target>  
PASS/FAIL per check  
Mistake category (if any)  
Fastest path: <commands>  
One-line takeaway.

strengths: Strong at high level: system design, cluster management with ArgoCD/GitOps, knows conceptually which object goes where.
Usually gets the Kubernetes part right (the pod/deployment/volume itself is correct).
weaknesses: Too slow: not fluent in imperative kubectl, searches docs for fields and flags.
Loses points on details, not knowledge.

mistakes_from_mock_exam.example: Created a ResourceQuota on cluster3 when the question was on cluster2 (context left over from the previous question).
Service named after the pod (webapp-svcn) instead of the required webapp-service-svcn - one wrong name failed 4 checks.
Helm installed with --generate-name instead of release name webapp-color-apd.
CronJob schedule '30 * * * *' (once an hour) instead of '*/30 * * * *' (every 30 min).
CronJob command split as [ps, -eaf] instead of [/bin/sh, -c, 'ps -eaf'] - grader looked for the string 'ps -eaf'.
EndpointSlice port had 'name: http' while the Service port was unnamed - ports pair by name, so the Service had no endpoints.
ConfigMap created with --from-file=<dir> instead of --from-env-file=<file> per file - keys were file names instead of KEY=value lines.
Wrote apiVersion as the CRD name (animes.animes.k8s.io/v1alpha1) instead of the group (animes.k8s.io/v1alpha1); copied field names with spaces from 'kubectl describe crd'.
Pasted a multi-line command onto one line with '\ ' left in - kubectl saw the flags as extra NAME arguments.
Created the Burstable pod but never wrote the required /root/qos_status_aecs file ('Also ...' sentence at the end of the task).
Wrote a fully correct secret-volume pod YAML but never ran kubectl apply (got side-tracked creating the secret).
Ran out of time on an easy liveness-probe question after spending too long debugging the EndpointSlice question.

exam_habits: First 30 seconds of the exam: alias k=kubectl; export do='--dry-run=client -o yaml'; export now='--force --grace-period=0'
EVERY question: copy-paste the 'kubectl config use-context ...' line FIRST, before reading the rest. Also when returning to an earlier question.
Read the whole task before typing. Turn it into a numbered checklist (names, namespace, values, every 'Also ...' sentence).
Copy names and values from the task text - never retype or 'improve' them (no v-prefix, no extra port names, no renamed headers).
Prefer: imperative command > imperative with $do into a file + small edit > writing YAML from scratch.
After every apply: k get <thing> (-o yaml | grep ...) and compare to the checklist. Not done until verified.
If stuck > 5-6 min, flag the question and move on. Easy low-weight questions first.
Field names: 'k explain pod.spec.containers.livenessProbe' (or --recursive) is faster than the docs. Never copy field names from 'kubectl describe' output.
Before submitting: loop over all contexts to find objects created on the wrong cluster: for c in $(k config get-contexts -o name); do echo == $c; k --context $c get <kind> -A | grep <name>; done

requirements: bash (WSL, Linux, macOS or Git Bash)
setup: ./lab.sh up            # cluster1 (kindnet) + cluster2 (Calico, enforces NetworkPolicy), metrics-server on both
./lab.sh setup <id>    # prepares one question on its cluster without changing your current context
./lab.sh reset         # start over from clean clusters
notes: Two clusters make the context-switching habit real. 'lab.sh setup' deliberately leaves your current context alone - switching is part of the drill.
NetworkPolicy traffic tests (netpol-02) run on cluster2, which has Calico.
Ingress questions are graded on the Ingress object; no ingress controller is installed.
Use ~/ instead of /root/ for output files.
Git Bash on Windows: run 'export MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1' first, otherwise arguments like /bin/sh are rewritten to Windows paths before reaching kubectl.exe and the object is silently wrong.

scenario_questions.task: Create a CronJob named simple-node-job in namespace ckad-job that uses image node and runs the command 'ps -eaf' using /bin/sh. The job must run every 30 minutes.

scenario_questions.inspired_by: Common CKAD: CronJob fields that have no imperative flag
scenario_questions.task: In namespace ckad-batch create a CronJob named report-cron with image busybox:1.36 that runs 'echo report' at 08:15 Monday to Friday. Concurrent runs must be forbidden, keep only 2 successful and 1 failed job in history, and each job must be terminated if it runs longer than 40 seconds.
verify: k get cj report-cron -n ckad-batch -o yaml | grep -E 'schedule|concurrency|HistoryLimit|activeDeadline'
fastest_solution: k create cronjob report-cron -n ckad-batch --image=busybox:1.36 --schedule="15 8 * * 1-5" $do -- /bin/sh -c "echo report" > cj.yaml
edit cj.yaml: add concurrencyPolicy, successfulJobsHistoryLimit, failedJobsHistoryLimit under CronJob spec; activeDeadlineSeconds under jobTemplate.spec
traps: activeDeadlineSeconds goes in jobTemplate.spec (the Job), not in the CronJob spec
Days of week: 0 = Sunday, 1-5 = Mon-Fri
scenario_questions.docs_search: k explain cronjob.spec ; k explain cronjob.spec.jobTemplate.spec

scenario_questions.inspired_by: Common CKAD: Job completions/parallelism
scenario_questions.task: Create a Job named batch-proc in namespace ckad-jobs with image busybox:1.36 that runs 'echo processing; sleep 3'. It must complete 6 times, running 2 pods in parallel, and give up after 3 failed retries.
verify: k get job batch-proc -n ckad-jobs -w   (wait for COMPLETIONS 6/6)

add completions: 6, parallelism: 2, backoffLimit: 3 under job spec (same level as template)
traps: restartPolicy must be Never or OnFailure (k create job sets Never)
These three fields sit under spec, not spec.template.spec

scenario_questions.inspired_by: FAILED: service to external webserver (EndpointSlice port name)
setup: docker rm -f ext-web >/dev/null 2>&1; docker run -d --name ext-web --network kind nginx >/dev/null
(tutor: tell the learner only that a webserver runs outside the cluster at that IP on port 80)

cat <<'EOF' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: external-webserver-svcn
  namespace: default
spec:
  ports:
  - port: 80
    protocol: TCP
    targetPort: 80
EOF
scenario_questions.task: A webserver runs outside the cluster at <IP> on port 80. Service external-webserver-svcn in namespace default should let pods reach it, but it does not work. Fix it so that other pods can use external-webserver-svcn to access the webserver. Do not delete the Service.
checks: endpoint port name matches the Service port name (here: unnamed)
curl from a pod to http://external-webserver-svcn returns the nginx page
verify: k describe svc external-webserver-svcn | grep Endpoints
fastest_solution:
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  name: external-webserver-svcn-1
  labels:
    kubernetes.io/service-name: external-webserver-svcn
addressType: IPv4
ports:
- port: 80
  protocol: TCP
endpoints:
- addresses:
  - <IP>
EOF
traps: The label kubernetes.io/service-name is the ONLY link between slice and Service (the slice name does not matter)
Port names must match exactly - unnamed Service port => no name on the slice port
Never use 127.0.0.1/localhost - in a pod that is the pod itself
Always check 'Endpoints:' in describe svc, then curl from a pod
variants: Service port is named 'web' (then the slice port MUST be named 'web')
use a legacy v1 Endpoints object instead (link = same name as Service)

grade.check: Service still exists and still has no selector
grade.cmd: kubectl --context cluster1 get svc external-webserver-svcn -n default -o json | jq -e  '.spec.selector == null'

grade.check: an EndpointSlice linked to the Service contains the webserver IP
grade.cmd: IP=$(docker inspect ext-web -f '{{.NetworkSettings.Networks.kind.IPAddress}}'); kubectl --context cluster1 get endpointslices -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=external-webserver-svcn -o json | jq -e --arg ip "$IP" '[.items[] | select(any(.endpoints[]?; any(.addresses[]; . == $ip)))] | length > 0'

grade.check: slice port is 80 and its name matches the Service port name exactly
grade.cmd: PN=$(kubectl --context cluster1 get svc external-webserver-svcn -n default -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].name}'); IP=$(docker inspect ext-web -f '{{.NetworkSettings.Networks.kind.IPAddress}}'); kubectl --context cluster1 get endpointslices -n default -l kubernetes.io/service-name=external-webserver-svcn -o json | jq -e --arg ip "$IP" --arg pn "$PN" '[.items[] | select(any(.endpoints[]?; any(.addresses[]; . == $ip))) | select(any(.ports[]; (.name // "") == $pn and .port == 80))] | length > 0'

grade.check: a pod can curl http://external-webserver-svcn and gets the nginx page
grade.cmd: kubectl --context cluster1 run grade-curl-$RANDOM -n default --rm -i --restart=Never --image=curlimages/curl -- curl -s -m 3 http://external-webserver-svcn 2>/dev/null | grep 'Welcome to nginx'

scenario_questions.task:
Create a pod named qos-pod-3 in namespace ckad17-qos with image nginx and container name qos-ctr-3. Configure it so it gets the QoS class Burstable. Also retrieve the name and QoS class of each Pod in namespace ckad17-qos in the format below and save it to ~/qos_status.

pod-1   qos_class
checks: pod qos-pod-3 exists with container name qos-ctr-3

scenario_questions.task: Create a NetworkPolicy db-allow-backend in namespace ckad-db that allows ingress to pods with label app=db only on TCP port 6379 and only from pods with label app=backend that run in namespaces labelled team=backend. All other ingress to the db pods must be blocked.
checks: ONE from-entry containing BOTH namespaceSelector team=backend AND podSelector app=backend
api pod can connect, other pod cannot
verify: k exec -n ckad-api api -- sh -c "echo PING | nc -w 2 $(k get pod db -n ckad-db -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}') 6379"   (expect +PONG)
k exec -n ckad-api other -- sh -c "echo PING | nc -w 2 $(k get pod db -n ckad-db -o jsonpath='{.status.podIP}') 6379"   (expect nothing / timeout)
fastest_solution:
cat <<EOF | k apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: db-allow-backend
  namespace: ckad-db
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: db
  policyTypes: [Ingress]
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          team: backend
      podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: backend
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 6379
EOF
traps: '- namespaceSelector' and '- podSelector' as two list items = OR (too open)
Same list item (no dash before podSelector) = AND

grading.philosophy: Graders are deliberately as harsh as the real exam grader: exact names, exact values, exact case, the question's cluster pinned with --context, and functional tests (curl/exec/can-i) where the real grader would run them. A question scores only the checks that print PASS.
grading.runner: ckad-grade.sh next to this file: ./ckad-grade.sh <question-id>  (or ./ckad-grade.sh all). Requires bash, kubectl, jq (and helm/docker for those questions).
grading.manual: Without the runner: run each grade[].cmd in bash; exit code 0 = PASS, anything else = FAIL.
grading.variants_rule: If the tutor changes names/values for a variant, the tutor MUST rewrite that question's grade commands with the new names and hand them to the learner before grading. Never grade a variant with the original commands.
